journey_stages.label: Attract
journey_stages.description: The customer discovers the business and becomes aware of its existence.

journey_stages.label: Engage
journey_stages.description: The customer evaluates the business, its value, and its experience.

journey_stages.label: Convert
journey_stages.description: The customer takes a meaningful action or becomes a customer/opportunity.

journey_stages.label: Retain
journey_stages.description: The business continues the relationship and creates additional value.

dimensions.label: Marketing Strategy
dimensions.description: Direction and market alignment: objectives, market opportunity, audience, positioning, offers, channels, priorities, and acquisition strategy.

dimensions.label: UX Design
dimensions.description: Experience and interaction: usability, navigation, information, digital experience, interactions, conversion paths, and friction.

dimensions.label: Brand Identity
dimensions.description: Meaning and expression: positioning, messaging, visual identity, verbal identity, differentiation, trust, relevance, and brand experience.

dimensions.label: Systems & Integration
dimensions.description: Infrastructure and connection: CRM, analytics, tracking, automation, data, technology, lead management, workflows, and integrations.

value.description: 1-5 maturity value; null only when applicability is not_applicable.

evidence.description: Supporting explanation. Separate from the score -- the deterministic engine does not reinterpret evidence to change the score.

levels.meaning: Improvement opportunity with limited immediate/systemic consequence
Meaningful weakness that may constrain performance
Significant weakness that may materially affect the journey or connected areas
Fundamental condition that may substantially prevent the relevant journey stage from functioning

derivation_rule.none_meaning: No negative severity is generated from this classification, regardless of impact level.
derivation_rule.depends_on: criteria[*].impact, which is fully assigned for all 51 criteria (EverCompass v1.0 final methodology decisions).

severity_model.note: Design Spec section 11. Severity is derived from classification x criterion impact (see derivation_rule), never from raw score alone. criteria[*].impact is fully assigned for all 51 criteria, so severity is computable end-to-end from this definition.

generation_rule.opportunity_note: The 'opportunity' finding type is never produced by this mapping. It is reserved for a future, explicit per-criterion override -- none of the 51 v1 criteria carry such an override.

finding_model.note: Design Spec section 10. Finding generation is a declarative classification_mapping (see generation_rule).

rule_types.v1_usage: Primary rule type for V1 -- used by all 51 criteria via classification_model.bands.

rule_types.description: Maps categorical responses to defined outcomes.
rule_types.v1_usage: Supported by the schema; not used by any V1 criterion (all 51 are maturity_1_5).

rule_types.description: Allows conditional evaluation and applicability logic.
rule_types.v1_usage: Supported by the schema; not used by any V1 criterion.

rule_types.description: Aggregates multiple criteria into a category/dimension score via weights.
rule_types.v1_usage: Reserved for future composite rules; not used in V1. No V1 criterion carries a weight field.
Deferred -- not implemented in V1 (Design Spec §8).

zero_applicable_criteria.note: Explicit edge case: no CRITICAL..OPERATIONALIZED condition is assigned when a dimension has zero applicable criteria.

high_impact_criterion_definition.scope: This definition applies ONLY to this dimension-level HIGH rule -- not reused elsewhere in the diagnostic definition.

method.evaluation_order_note: Rules are evaluated top to bottom (critical first); the first matching condition wins.

dimension.note: Design Spec section 13: 'not a simple average'. Resolved as declarative condition rules -- see method. Preserves distribution/pattern info; never reduces to a number.

insufficient_applicable_criteria.note: Explicit edge case for a journey stage whose underlying dimensions have insufficient applicable criteria to determine a condition. Exact threshold for 'insufficient' beyond the zero-applicable-per-dimension case is not specified -- needs confirmation, see ambiguity log.

method.evaluation_order_note: Rules are evaluated top to bottom (critical first); the first matching condition wins.

journey.note: Design Spec section 14. Resolved as declarative condition rules over the journey's four dimensions -- see method. Never averages dimension scores; preserves dimension-level information.

aggregation.overall_score_note: V1 deliberately does not reduce the entire business to a single number (Design Spec §20).

scoring_formula.usage: Internal ordering only. Never exposed as an 'EverCompass Score' or a single business health score.
depends_on: criteria[*].impact -- fully assigned for all 51 criteria (EverCompass v1.0 final methodology decisions).

The concentration category (isolated/repeated/concentrated/systemic) is now determined by concentration_determination_rule's explicit thresholds (see above). What remains open, as a separate dependency: what makes a set of findings 'related' in the first place (Design Spec section 15, Pattern) -- these thresholds operate on a related-findings set once one exists.

journey_relevance is fixed at "high" (journey_relevance_weight = 3) for every criterion in EverCompass v1.0, not derived via a categorization rule -- every criterion is intentionally assigned to one journey stage and evaluates a condition directly relevant to it. "Critical" is deliberately withheld at the criterion-definition level so criticality arises from evaluated diagnostic conditions, not an assumed foundational status. A differentiated categorization rule may be introduced in a later diagnostic version -- see journey_relevance_model.note.
scoring_formula.relationship_to_precedence_order: This numeric formula operationalizes the qualitative precedence_order/tie_breakers above (Design Spec section 17) into a single sortable number; both describe the same v1 priority principle, not two competing ones.

systemic.note: Systemic represents a broader system-spanning pattern, not merely a large count -- either condition alone qualifies.

concentration_determination_rule.depends_on: What makes a set of findings 'related' in the first place (Design Spec section 15, Pattern) is not defined by this instruction and remains a separate, unresolved dependency -- these thresholds operate on a related-findings set once one exists.

scoring_formula.v1_note: journey_relevance is uniformly "high" (weight 3) for all v1 criteria -- see journey_relevance_model.note. Effective v1 priority differentiation therefore comes primarily from severity, impact, and concentration, not journey_relevance. journey_relevance is kept in the formula and schema (not removed) for later diagnostic versions.

priority.note: Design Spec sections 16-18. scoring_formula is a declarative weighted product. criteria[*].impact is fully assigned and journey_relevance is fixed at "high" for v1.0, so priority is computable end-to-end from this definition except for the concentration dependency noted in scoring_formula.depends_on (what makes findings "related" in the first place remains open). Root-cause inference remains deferred beyond V1.

criteria.question: How clearly defined is the audience your business is trying to attract?
How clearly does the business communicate why a customer should choose it over alternatives?
How intentionally does the business select and use channels to reach its target audience?
How clearly has the business defined how it will turn its target audience into potential customers?
How effectively does the business's digital experience help a new visitor understand what the business offers and where to go next?
How effectively do the business's landing pages connect a visitor's initial interest to a clear and relevant next step?
How effectively are the business's entry points designed to move visitors from initial discovery into the customer journey?
How effectively does the business establish awareness of its brand among the audience it wants to reach?
How clearly does the business communicate what makes it meaningfully different from alternatives?
How clearly does the business communicate its value and relevance to the audience it wants to attract?
How effectively does the business capture the information needed to understand where its customer acquisition activity is coming from and how it is performing?
How effectively can the business determine which acquisition sources and activities are contributing to customer opportunities?
How effectively does the business's underlying infrastructure support the acquisition of new customers and opportunities?
How clearly does the business's offer address a meaningful need or opportunity for its intended audience?
How clearly does the business communicate the value a customer can expect from choosing its offer?
How intentionally does the business use content to help its audience evaluate the business, its offer, and its value?
How effectively does the business's website experience help visitors evaluate the business and move toward the next appropriate step?
How effectively does the business's navigation help visitors find the information they need to evaluate the business?
How effectively does the business provide the information customers need to evaluate its offering and make an informed decision?
How effectively does the business's brand experience establish trust as customers evaluate the business?
How clearly does the brand communicate what the business offers and what customers can expect?
How effectively does the brand communicate in a way that feels relevant to the audience's needs, priorities, and situation?
How consistently does the customer's experience reflect the brand's intended identity, value, and expectations?
How effectively does the business use analytics to understand what happens as potential customers evaluate the business?
How effectively does the business capture the information needed to understand and manage customers as they evaluate the business?
How effectively does the business connect customer and prospect information to the systems used to manage relationships and opportunities?
How intentionally has the business designed the process for turning engaged prospects into customers or meaningful opportunities?
How effectively does the offer give an engaged prospect a clear and compelling reason to take the next meaningful action?
How effectively are marketing and sales aligned around converting qualified prospects into customers or opportunities?
How effectively does the user experience guide an engaged prospect toward completing the intended conversion action?
How effectively do the business's forms support prospects in completing the intended conversion action?
How effectively does the booking experience help a prospect complete the intended conversion with minimal friction?
How effectively does the checkout experience help a prospect complete a purchase with clarity and minimal friction?
How effectively does the brand communicate the value of the offer at the point where a prospect is deciding whether to take action?
How effectively does the brand provide credible signals that support a prospect's decision to take action?
How effectively does the brand experience give prospects the confidence they need to take the intended action?
How effectively does the business move new leads or opportunities to the appropriate person, process, or next step?
How effectively does the business follow up with prospects after they take a conversion-related action?
How effectively does the business measure whether conversion activities are producing the intended customer or business outcomes?
How intentionally does the business continue to create meaningful value for existing customers?
How intentionally does the business encourage existing customers to continue their relationship with the business?
How intentionally does the business manage ongoing customer relationships across the customer lifecycle?
How effectively does the ongoing customer experience support satisfaction, continued value, and the relationship with the business?
How effectively are ongoing account or service interactions designed to make it easy for customers to manage their relationship with the business?
How intentionally does the brand support and strengthen its ongoing relationship with existing customers?
How intentionally does the brand encourage customers to maintain an ongoing preference and relationship with the business?
How effectively does the brand remain relevant to existing customers as their needs, expectations, and relationship with the business evolve?
How effectively does the business use its CRM or relationship-management system to support ongoing customer relationships?
How effectively does the business use automation to support ongoing customer relationships and lifecycle activities?
How effectively does the business communicate with customers according to their stage, needs, and relationship with the business?
How effectively does the business maintain and use customer data to understand and support ongoing customer relationships?

journey_relevance_model.note: Design Spec priority signals + this session's decision. Must be explicitly defined on the diagnostic criteria/configuration where required -- never inferred by the engine from question wording. v1.0: uniformly "high" for all 51 criteria -- every criterion is intentionally assigned to one specific journey stage and evaluates a condition directly relevant to it. Not varied merely to create scoring differentiation; "critical" is deliberately not used at the criterion-definition level in v1.0 -- criticality should arise from evaluated diagnostic conditions, not from assuming a criterion is always foundational. journey_relevance_weight is therefore 3 for every v1 criterion. The field and weight model are retained for later diagnostic versions that may introduce differentiated cross-journey/root-cause relevance.
